texts.preamble: Harjeet Singh Kumar vs Shikha Kumar on 4 March, 2025 In The Court Of Ms. Sheetal Chaudhary Pradhan Additional Sessions Judge-02, South-East District Saket Courts, New Delhi Criminal Appeal No. 262/2024 Ps- New Friends Colony U/Sec. 29 Pwdv Act In the matter of :
texts.facts: This is an appeal U/Sec. 29 of the Protection Protection of Woman from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (hereinafter referred to as 'DV Act') against the order dated 12.10.2023 (hereinafter referred to as 'impugned order') passed by Ld. Trial Court in CT Case No. 2684/2020 titled as "Shikha Kumar Vs. Harjeet Singh Kumar" whereby Ld. Trial Court has passed interim order and appellant no. 1 (husband) herein was directed to pay interim maintenance of Rs. 50,000/- to the complainant from the date of filing of petition i.e. 18.03.2020 till the disposal of the case. Harjeet Singh Kumar vs Shikha Kumar on 4 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179428829/ 1 2. In order to avoid any confusion, both the parties shall be referred with the same nomenclature with which they were referred before the Ld. Trial Court, in my subsequent paragraphs. 3. As per record of Ld. Trial Court, the brief facts necessary for disposal of present appeal, are as follows :- "That the marriage between the complainant and respondent Harjeet Singh Kumar was solemnized on 20.01.2012 and both the parties are marriage lived in the matrimonial home. That family of complainant has spent huge amount of money of Rs. 18 Lacs (approximately) in the marriage. Further, that family of husband of complainant was well aware of the fact that complainant had two minor children from her CA No. 262/2024 Harjeet Singh Kumar Vs. Shikha Kumar Page no. 2 of 14 first marriage and also the marriage of respondent Harjeet Singh Kumar was the second marriage with the complainant herein. After marriage, in November 2011, respondent/ husband with hand in glove with other respondents had made demands qua property and share of money following demands of dowry articles from complainant and her family. However, soon after marriage, the family of the respondent along-with respondents ill treated the complainant. The behaviour of the respondents were extremely rude towards the complainant and quarrel between them were started. After the marriage, complainant has witnessed the illicit affair with a man and marriage certificate of respondent/husband with another woman namely Deepti Arora, dated 26.12.2023. It has been alleged that husband of complainant with an dishonest intention transferred an huge amount from the account of complainant to his account or used it for his own use. It has been stated that respondents humiliate, harassed and tortured complainant and thereafter, being a helpless woman, complainant lodged an FIR No.37/2020 u/sec.498A/406/34 IPC PS NFC against respondents. It has been prayed that maintenance of Rs. 2,11,900/- per month be granted for herself and her sons". CA No. 262/2024 Harjeet Singh Kumar Vs. Shikha Kumar Page no. 3 of 14 4. Vide order dated 12.10.2023, Ld. Trial Court has awarded Rs.50,000/- per month as interim maintenance towards the complainant payable by respondent from the date of filing of petition i.e. 18.03.2020 till its disposal. 5. Aggrieved to the aforesaid impugned order dated 12.10.2023 passed by Ld. Trial Court, respondent has challenged the said order by way of present appeal, on the following grounds :- a) The impugned order is completely basis on concocted and frivolous facts wherein the true facts were not appreciated while passing the above mentioned Order. b) That impugned order, would establish that Ld. Trial Court passed order, solely relying on the submissions of the Respondent, which is not supported by any prima facie evidence or attending circumstances. The sole basis of passing the order was Harjeet Singh Kumar vs Shikha Kumar on 4 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179428829/ 2 perusal of bank account statements and credit entries of all the bank accounts of the Appellant No.1, which was derived based on false and frivolous facts as the credit entries are borrowings and debt received from various sources and that, under no circumstances can they be classified as income or profit earned. CA No. 262/2024 Harjeet Singh Kumar Vs. Page no. 4 of 14 c) That respondent/ complainant is not liable to receive maintenance from the Appellant/ husband as she earning Rs.2,63,992/- per month being the Vice President, in Innova ESI Private Ltd, which is more than the salary of the Appellant No.1 and the Respondent, is self-sufficient to take care of her day to day expenses including food, clothing, rent and other miscellaneous expenses. d) That appellant/ husband is only earning Rs. 2,00,000 per month out of which he has to spend a hefty amount to the tune of Rs.1,00,000 per month which is 50% of his salary towards medical expenses as he is suffering from kidney tumour and he already finds it very difficult to manage his day to day expenses. e) That appellant/ husband's monthly expenses amount to Rs.2,50,000 which exceeds his monthly income and he has to take care of his old aged mother as well through the limited amount that he earns and therefore he has to take loans from different institutions including friends and family to make ends meet. f) That appellant/ husband is already under heavy debt from friends and family which causes a lot of mental stress and trauma to the Appellant/ husband is not financially capable to pay maintenance to the Respondent amounting to Rs. 50,000/- per month under any given circumstances. CA No. 262/2024 Harjeet Singh Kumar Vs. Shikha Kumar Page no. 5 of 14 g) That Respondent/ complainant has failed to give any prudent justification towards the expenses claimed by her in the Sec 12 and Sec 23 Application under the DV Act as mandated by the Apex Court of India.
texts.arguments: 6. In addition, Ld. Counsel for respondent/ husband has argued that impugned order is vitiated by fatal infirmities and has argued that impugned order dated 12.10.2023 passed by Ld. Trial Court, is not in accordance with law. He has further argued that immense irreparable damage and loss would be caused to the appellant/ husband, if the present appeal is not allowed. It is prayed that impugned order dated 12.10.2023 passed by Ld. Trial Court, is liable to [LEAKAGE_MASK]. On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for complainant/ respondent herein has argued that impugned order passed by Ld. Trial Court, is legally correct and needs no interference and it has been passed after considering the documents and evidence on record and he is having income of more than Rs. 10 Lakh per month besides that he is also having various assets including properties. Further all the stridhan articles/jewellery and documents are in the possession of respondents and it is the complainant who has been suffering mental agony at the hands of the respondents. 10. The Act inter-alia provides for more effective protection or the right of woman guaranteed under the constitution who are victims of the domestic violence of any kind occurring within the shared household. According to the Act, any harm, injury to health, safety, life, limb or well being or any other act or threatening or coercion etc. by any adult member of the family, constitutes domestic violence. Further, the act also contemplates that any woman who is or has been in a domestic relationship, if she is subjected to any domestic violence can file a complaint u/sec. 12 of the PWDV Act. This Act also covers those woman who are or have been in relationship with the abuser where both parties have live together in a shared household and a relative by consanguinity, marriage or through a relationship in the nature of marriage or adoption. CA No. 262/2024 Harjeet Singh Kumar Vs. Shikha Kumar Page no. 8 of 14 Harjeet Singh Kumar vs Shikha Kumar on 4 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179428829/ This section of the Act allows Magistrates to order compensation and damages for injuries caused by domestic violence. Section 3 of the Act defines domestic violence, encompassing acts or conduct that harm or endanger the victim's health, safety, or well-being. The Domestic Violence Act explicitly states that domestic violence includes actions aimed at coercing the aggrieved person or her relatives to meet unlawful dowry demands or surrender property or valuable security. The Act defines an "aggrieved person" as any woman who is currently or has been in a domestic relationship with the respondent. Harjeet Singh Kumar vs Shikha Kumar on 4 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179428829/ 5 12. At the same time, Section 20 of the Domestic Violence Act allows magistrates to order monetary relief to meet expenses and losses suffered by the aggrieved person and any children, aligning with their accustomed standard of living. Further the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of Chaturbhuj vs. Sita Bai AIR 2008 Supreme Court 530, emphasized preventing destitution in maintenance proceedings rather than punishing neglectful spouses. The Supreme Court's rulings in cases like Kalyan Dey Chowdhury vs. Rita Dey Chowdhury Nee Nandy and Dr. Kulbhushan Kumar vs. Raj Kumari provide guidelines for determining maintenance amounts based on parties' status and capacity to pay. Therefore, in my considered view, the Court has discretionary powers CA No. 262/2024 Harjeet Singh Kumar Vs. Shikha Kumar Page no. 11 of 14 in computing damages, considering both the victim's suffering and the parties' financial status. The court acknowledges the absence of clear precedents in calculating damages while awarding compensation to the aggrieved person. The debate surrounding compensation criteria reflects the nuanced balancing act between addressing victims' needs and ensuring fairness in legal proceedings.
